questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: São Paulo is the economic center of Latin America. Furthermore, USP is ranked the best university in Latin America.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: USP is difficult to arrive to. Luckily, the international coordinator was helpfull in guiding me when choosing which faculties to study at. Be aware that USP has various campus and they are spread all over the state.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: My faculty (FFLCH) hosted a welcome week. I recieved valuable information and met many other exchange students. Be aware that the welcome week orientation is in Portuguese. However, one can attend classes taught in English at USP.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it difficult to find housing. The city is expensive for Latin America and there are many bureaucratic obstacles when renting. I would recommend to search "Republicas da USP" on Facebook for shared living.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Don´t live in the old city center. It is dangerous. I would recommend to find shared living through facebook or pages such as "webquarto".

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is not any housing available.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Once you get accepted you need to apply for courses. The courses that USP has online are old courses and the new courses will not be posted until very last minute. Therefore, you must apply to courses that won´t be offered. However, the faculty you apply to will still be your host faculty and will facilitate everything on your behalf (even if you end up not taking courses there afterall). I recommend to apply for courses from only one faculty and to choose a faculty you are most interested in. Be aware that as an exchange student you can attend all faculties and attend very different classes, so enjoy this opportunity.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is an international coordinatior from USP that can help you. Once you have applied to a specific faculty, their international department will be your point of contact.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It is very confusing to get an overview of the classes available. You will need to spend a long time to crosscheck different faculties´ courses and to see the level of the course. When you wish to register you can email the professor directly or the international department of the faculty of the course. They are very flecxible to exchange students and I was allowed to do my exam in English even though the class was in Portuguese.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: See above

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses have the same level as in Denmark. Be aware that attendance is mandatory. Most master classes are 4 hours long and the teacher expects discussions among the students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: UCPH is more flexible. Studying at USP is more like attending high school in Denmark, where the participation in class can affect your final grade and attendance is mandatory.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
EAD5933 - Geopolitics and Corporate Strategy
FLS6195 - Cities, government and public policies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you do not speak Portuguese, I would recommend you to look at the courses offered by FEA. They have many courses in English.

questions.answer: I didn´t have unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food at USP is very cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is great amount of sport activities that you can do for free. There is a free cinema showing movies every day and there are many museums which are free.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Participate in sports.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Try the parties in USP, enjoy the city and its museums, visit the neighbourhood of Liberdade, go to the beaches.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The Brazilian people is very warm and kind. Even though I don´t speak Portuguese I did not have any problems getting by with Spanish and English. At USP many speak English and in São Paulo you will also find many people who speak English. However, the majority do not speak English.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the parties at USP. There are parties every weekend.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn´t find anything challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Warm people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1: Only apply to courses from one faculty when seeking your acceptance at USP (to avoid bureaucratic chaos). 
2: Join the parties.
3: Eat in the local restaurant. Food is only 2,5 DKK.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make your appointment to the federal police already when you arrive. Later they have a long waiting time and you will need the document from the police to apply for the cheaper buscard.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Good parties and great friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language barrier.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
